headline: KKR Exits First Gen in ₱25.77-Billion Share Sale
seoTitle: KKR Exits First Gen in ₱25.77-Billion Share Sale | FMB News
seoDescription: KKR sold its entire 19.9% interest in Philippine power producer First Gen for about ₱25.77 billion, ending a six-year investment in the company.
deck: The global investment firm sold its entire 19.9% stake in First Gen for about ₱25.77 billion, ending a six-year investment in one of the Philippines’ major power producers.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: KKR sold its entire interest in First Gen Corp., disposing of about 715.9 million shares representing a 19.9% stake in the Philippine power producer.
Reuters reported the transaction value at approximately ₱25.77 billion, or about $410 million. The buyer was Angsana Finance Limited.
The sale ends KKR’s roughly six-year investment in First Gen.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The divestment follows an earlier attempt by KKR to increase its position in First Gen. The company’s parent had rejected a proposal that could have led to a broader acquisition process.
First Gen operates a portfolio that includes natural-gas and renewable-energy assets and is a significant participant in the Philippine electricity market.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Large ownership changes in major power producers matter because the energy sector requires substantial long-term capital and plays a direct role in electricity supply and investment planning.

The transaction is also a notable foreign-investment exit from a major Philippine listed company, although the sale itself does not imply a change in First Gen’s operating assets or electricity supply.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for ownership disclosures, any subsequent strategic moves by First Gen or its parent, and whether the new shareholder signals a longer-term role in the company.

verificationNotes: Reuters and Forbes corroborate the sale of KKR’s entire 19.9% interest, approximately 715.9 million shares, for about ₱25.8 billion.
The article does not infer operational changes at First Gen from the ownership transaction alone.
